info.description: REST API for the MCP Data Platform. Covers admin endpoints (system, config, personas, auth keys, audit, knowledge, memory, connections), portal endpoints (assets, collections, shares, prompts, activity), and resource management.
info.title: MCP Data Platform API

get.description: Returns all API catalogs with derived spec_count and ref_count fields.

post.description: Creates a new API catalog. Only available in database config mode.

get.description: Returns a single API catalog by ID with derived spec_count and ref_count fields.

put.description: Applies a partial edit to a catalog and reloads dependent api-gateway connections.

delete.description: Deletes a catalog. Rejected with 409 if any connection still references it.

post.description: Creates a new catalog by copying the source catalog's metadata, specs, and embeddings.

get.description: Returns the per-catalog embedding roll-up (specs total/indexed/pending/running/failed).
Returns recent embedding job rows for a catalog, optionally filtered by status and spec_name.
Returns one row per spec with operation_count, embedding_count, and latest job state.
Returns the specs in a catalog with embedding metadata. Spec content is omitted.
Returns a single catalog spec including its content and embedding metadata.

put.description: Creates or updates a catalog spec from inline content or a fetched URL, then enqueues an embedding job.

delete.description: Removes a spec from a catalog and reloads dependent api-gateway connections.

get.description: Returns the operations a catalog spec parses to. The spec document is not returned.
Returns one operation's parameters, request body and per-status responses. The spec document is not returned.

post.description: Enqueues a manual_retry embedding job for a spec, recomputing vectors fresh without the text-hash dedup.
Re-fetches a URL-sourced spec from its source_url, stores the new content, and enqueues an embedding job.

put.description: Stores a catalog spec from a multipart file upload, then enqueues an embedding job.

post.description: Generates a PKCE verifier, derives the SHA256 challenge, registers a state token, and returns the authorization URL the operator should open in their browser. The upstream IdP redirects back to /api/v1/admin/api-gateway/oauth/callback after the user authenticates.
post.summary: Begin OAuth authorization-code flow for an API gateway connection

get.description: Public endpoint hit by the upstream IdP after the operator authenticates. Exchanges the code for tokens and persists them via the API gateway's TokenStore. Renders an HTML error page on failure so a stranded browser tab still gives a useful message.
get.summary: OAuth authorization-code callback for API gateway connections

get.description: Returns every api-kind connection this deployment serves with the operations its catalog declares, narrowed by no persona. Backs the persona editor's API-endpoint scope, where an operator selects operations to allow or deny.
get.summary: List the API operations persona rules can name

get.description: Returns all platform assets without owner restriction, with active share summaries.
Returns a single asset by ID without owner restriction.

put.description: Updates an asset's metadata (name, description, tags) without owner restriction.

delete.description: Soft-deletes an asset without owner restriction.

get.description: Streams an asset's stored S3 content without owner restriction.

put.description: Replaces an asset's stored content from the raw request body and records a new version.

get.description:
Streams an asset's PNG thumbnail without owner restriction. The
dark variant falls back to the light image for content types
that carry their own colors and store only one.

put.description: Stores a PNG thumbnail for an asset from the raw request body.

get.description: Returns the version history for an asset.
Streams the stored content for a specific asset version.

post.description: Creates a new asset version by reverting to a previous version's content.

The event kinds it returns are the ones this deployment has actually produced, which is what the event_kind filter on the other audit endpoints should be driven from.
Returns a single audit event by ID.
Returns audit event counts grouped by a dimension.

parameters.description: Dimension: tool_name, user_id, persona, toolkit_kind, connection
parameters.name: group_by

parameters.description: Filter by event kind: admin, mcp_tool_call, apigateway_invoke, prompt_serve, resource_read, resource_move, script_run. GET /admin/audit/events/filters returns the kinds present in the data.
parameters.name: event_kind

get.description: Returns discovery-before-query session pattern statistics.

parameters.description: Filter by event kind: admin, mcp_tool_call, apigateway_invoke, prompt_serve, resource_read, resource_move, script_run. GET /admin/audit/events/filters returns the kinds present in the data.
parameters.name: event_kind

get.description: Returns aggregate enrichment statistics including mode breakdown and token savings.

parameters.description: Filter by event kind: admin, mcp_tool_call, apigateway_invoke, prompt_serve, resource_read, resource_move, script_run. GET /admin/audit/events/filters returns the kinds present in the data.
parameters.name: event_kind

get.description: Returns aggregate audit statistics for the given time range.

parameters.description: Filter by event kind: admin, mcp_tool_call, apigateway_invoke, prompt_serve, resource_read, resource_move, script_run. GET /admin/audit/events/filters returns the kinds present in the data.
parameters.name: event_kind

get.description: Returns latency percentile statistics for the given time range.

parameters.description: Filter by event kind: admin, mcp_tool_call, apigateway_invoke, prompt_serve, resource_read, resource_move, script_run. GET /admin/audit/events/filters returns the kinds present in the data.
parameters.name: event_kind

get.description: Returns audit event counts bucketed by time resolution.

parameters.description: Time bucket resolution: minute, hour, day (default: hour)
parameters.name: resolution

parameters.description: Filter by event kind: admin, mcp_tool_call, apigateway_invoke, prompt_serve, resource_read, resource_move, script_run. GET /admin/audit/events/filters returns the kinds present in the data.

get.description: Returns aggregate counts for total, successful, and failed events. Supports time and filter parameters.

parameters.description: Filter by event kind: admin, mcp_tool_call, apigateway_invoke, prompt_serve, resource_read, resource_move, script_run. GET /admin/audit/events/filters returns the kinds present in the data.
parameters.name: event_kind

get.description: Returns all API keys (key values are never exposed, only names and roles).

post.description: Generates a new API key. The key value is returned only once.

delete.description: Deletes an API key.

get.description: Returns every data-access call the platform recorded, newest first: each query and API invocation with the purpose stated for it, the outcome derived from what was built from it, and how many later sessions re-ran it. Set queue=promotable for the review queue, which keeps the records that answered something and orders them by reuse first.

parameters.description: Filter by outcome (failed, satisfied, superseded, ran)
parameters.name: outcome

parameters.description: Filter by a dataset URN or endpoint the call addressed
parameters.name: target

parameters.description: Match the purpose or the statement
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Set to 'promotable' for the review queue
parameters.name: queue

get.description: Returns one call record whoever made it: the statement or request line, the purpose stated for it, its outcome and how it was reached, the assets and captures built from it, and how many later sessions re-ran it.

post.description: Publishes a satisfied record: a query becomes a Query entity in the data catalog, associated with every dataset it reads; an API call becomes a saved example on its endpoint. The record then carries what it became and who promoted it.
Records that a reviewer decided this record is not worth publishing, with an optional note, so the review queue stops offering it.

get.description: Returns all asset collections without owner restriction, with active share summaries.

parameters.description: Search term matching name, description, or owner email
parameters.name: search

get.description: Returns a single asset collection by ID, with its sections and items, without owner restriction.

put.description: Updates an asset collection's name and/or description without owner restriction.

delete.description: Soft-deletes an asset collection without owner restriction. The assets it holds are not deleted.

get.description: Returns the current configuration as JSON with sensitive values redacted.

Returns the platform-owned instruction baseline (#646) for this deployment — the "how to operate" guidance composed beneath the admin's agent_instructions. It names only tools registered on this platform, so admins can see what the platform already covers and write business context rather than restating the operating model.
Returns a page of config change history entries, newest first, with the total count.
Returns the merged config view: for each whitelisted key, the database override if present, otherwise the file default.
Returns all database-backed config override entries.
Returns a single database-backed config override entry by key.

put.description: Creates or updates a database-backed config override entry. The stored value is authoritative and is in force on every replica from the next read.

delete.description: Removes a database-backed config override entry. Subsequent reads on every replica fall through to the file-config default.

get.description: Returns the current configuration as downloadable YAML. Sensitive values are redacted by default.

parameters.description: Set to 'true' to include sensitive values
parameters.name: secrets

get.description: Returns the current config store mode (file or database).
Returns all database-managed connection instances.
Returns the merged view of file-configured (live) and database-managed connection instances, with secrets redacted.
Returns a single database-managed connection instance by kind and name.

put.description: Creates or updates a database-managed connection instance. A connection the platform configuration file declares is refused with 409: the file owns it.

delete.description: Deletes a database-managed connection instance. A connection the platform configuration file declares is refused with 409: the file owns it.

get.description: Returns all toolkit connections with their tools.

Single-shot per-connection OAuth health used by the connection-list view to render a per-row health badge. Returns has_oauth=false for non-OAuth connections so the UI doesn't have to filter client-side.
get.summary: Bulk OAuth health for all connections
OAuth lifecycle history for a connection

post.description: Validates the connection is configured for authorization_code OAuth, generates a PKCE verifier, registers a state token (with kind), and returns the authorization URL the operator should open in their browser. Works for any connection kind registered in OAuthKinds.
post.summary: Begin OAuth authorization-code flow for any connection
Force a refresh-token exchange for a connection

get.description: Returns the configured embedding provider's kind, model, dimension, and a status enum (ok / unconfigured). Used by the portal to surface a banner when semantic features are disabled.

get.summary: List enrichment rules for a connection

post.description: Loads the rule, applies it against the provided sample args/response/user without persisting and without invoking the live gateway, and returns the merged response + per-rule trace. Use this in the rule editor to validate bindings and merge strategy.

Generates a PKCE verifier, derives the SHA256 challenge, registers a state token, and returns the authorization URL the operator should open in their browser. The platform expects the upstream to redirect to /api/v1/admin/oauth/callback after the user authenticates.
post.summary: Begin OAuth authorization-code flow for a gateway connection

post.description: Triggers a client_credentials grant against the configured OAuth token URL, replacing the cached token. Used to recover from upstream-side credential rotations or to verify the configured client_id/client_secret without waiting for token expiry.
post.summary: Force a fresh OAuth token exchange

post.description: Re-dials a configured gateway connection using the stored config, re-discovers its tool set, and swaps the live connection atomically. Used after an upstream adds, removes, or changes tools.

get.description: Reports whether the connection is healthy, its tool count, and (when AuthMode=oauth) the current token state — expiry, last refreshed, last error.
get.summary: Get a gateway connection's runtime status

post.description: Tests a gateway connection by listing its tools. When a connection with this name is already registered in the live toolkit AND has an active upstreamClient, the request body is IGNORED and the live client (with its loaded TokenStore + auth round-tripper) is exercised — green proves real tool calls would work right now. When no live client exists for this name (the connection is unregistered, OR it's a placeholder awaiting first OAuth Connect, OR a prior dial left it without a client), falls back to a one-shot dial against the submitted config (preview-before-save semantics). The redacted-field merge from the stored config only applies to the fallback path. Does not persist anything.

get.description: Returns embedding-provider health plus a per-kind rollup (job-state counts, last activity, coverage) for every registered index_jobs consumer. Renders an empty kinds list when no queue is wired.

post.description: Resolves every open failed job for one unit, clearing it from the triage surface. The explicit fallback for a failure that will never be superseded (e.g. a removed consumer's leftover rows). Idempotent: dismissing an already-clean unit returns 200 with resolved=0.

get.description: Returns the units with open (unresolved) failures, one entry per unit, most-recently-failed first, with first/last-seen timestamps and last-success context. A failure leaves this set automatically once a later job for the same unit succeeds, or when an operator dismisses it.
Returns index_jobs rows newest first, filterable by kind, status, and source_id. Used by the dashboard's in-flight, retry/backoff, and failure-triage views.

post.description: Enqueues manual-retry jobs for a kind. With source_id it targets one unit; without, every out-of-sync unit. Mirrors the api-catalog manual-retry action across all kinds.

get.description: Returns paginated changesets with optional filtering.
Returns a single changeset by ID.

post.description:
Reverts the DataHub aspects a changeset mutated back to their pre-change
state, transitions the source insights to rolled_back, and marks the
changeset rolled back. Refused (409) when already rolled back or when a
newer changeset has since touched the same aspect, and (422) when the
changeset contains change types whose prior state was not captured.

get.description: Returns paginated insights with optional filtering.

parameters.description: Sort by created_at: 'oldest' for oldest-first, default newest-first
parameters.name: order

get.description: Returns aggregated insight statistics by entity, category, confidence, and status.
Returns a single insight by ID.

put.description: Update insight text, category, or confidence. Cannot edit an applied insight.
Approve or reject an insight. Status must be 'approved' or 'rejected'.

get.description: Returns paginated notification queue rows, newest first, with delivery status, attempt count, and failure detail. Bounded by the queue's retention window rather than being a full archive.

parameters.description: Filter by status (pending, sending, sent, failed)
parameters.name: status

get.description: Returns per-status notification counts and the retention window they cover. The recipient and category filters apply; status does not, so a status-filtered list still shows the full breakdown.

Public endpoint hit by the upstream OAuth provider after the operator authenticates. Exchanges the code for tokens and stores them. Renders an HTML page on error so a stranded browser tab still gives a useful message.
Returns all configured personas with tool counts.

post.description: Creates a new persona. Only available in database config mode.

get.description: Returns a single persona with resolved tool list.

put.description: Updates an existing persona. Only available in database config mode.

delete.description: Deletes a persona. Only available in database config mode. Cannot delete the admin persona.

post.description: Evaluates the named persona's rules and returns the decision with what produced it. With tool_name set it answers the tool question and returns the matching pattern. With connection set it answers whether the persona may invoke method on path of that api-kind connection and returns the matching API route rule.
post.summary: Preview a persona's decision for a tool or an API route

get.description: Returns every prompt collection with its member prompt count, ordered by name.

post.description: Creates a named collection organizing the prompt library. Names are unique case-insensitively.

put.description: Renames or re-describes a collection.

delete.description: Deletes a collection; member prompts are released to the default (uncollected) group.

get.description: Returns all prompts across all scopes, including system-registered prompts. Supports scope, search, and owner_email filters.

post.description: Creates a new prompt and registers it with the live MCP server when enabled. A global or persona prompt created here lands approved, with the creating admin stamped as its approver.

get.description: Returns run count and last-run timestamp per prompt id, aggregated from prompt_serve audit events within the audit retention window. Prompts never served are absent from the map.
Returns a single prompt by ID.

put.description: Updates an existing prompt by ID and re-registers it with the live MCP server. A content or arguments edit to an approved global or persona prompt is deferred as a pending draft version (202): the approved snapshot keeps being served until the draft is approved via the version approval endpoint.

delete.description: Deletes a prompt by ID and unregisters it from the live MCP server.

post.description: Approves a personal prompt's pending promotion request, moving it to the requested persona/global scope and marking it approved.

put.description: Places a prompt in a collection, or clears the assignment with an empty collection_id. Placement is organizational metadata: no version is produced and no review is triggered.

post.description: Clears a personal prompt's pending promotion request, leaving it personal.

get.description: Returns every version of a prompt with full content and author, newest first.
Returns a single prompt version snapshot.

post.description: Applies a pending draft version's snapshot to the live prompt, stamping the approval on that specific version. Other pending drafts are superseded.
Rejects a pending draft version, leaving the live prompt unchanged.

get.description: Returns every managed script with its lifecycle status and current version.

Returns recent runs across every script, newest first, with what triggered each one, how it ended, how long it took, and how many outputs it produced. The operator view of what the platform has been running unattended.
Returns every managed-script schedule with its cadence, its bound parameters, its next fire, and how many fires it has missed.
Returns the cadence a script runs on, the parameters every fire binds, when it fires next, and how many fires it has missed.

put.description: Creates or replaces the cadence a script runs on. The parameters are validated against the script's contract. A schedule grants no authority: every fire executes the latest saved version, authorized against the roles captured at that save.

post.description: Stops a schedule firing, keeping the row that explains the runs it produced. There is deliberately no way to delete a schedule.
Resumes a paused schedule without touching its cadence. The next fire is the one it was parked on, which the misfire policy then collapses to a single run — the same treatment downtime gets.

get.description: Returns every version of a script with its source, its author, and the roles that author held.
Returns one version's snapshot together with the capabilities, connections, and destinations its source reaches for.

Returns sessions derived from the audit log, most recently active first. A session is not a stored row: it is every audit event sharing one session id, so the list reaches as far back as audit retention.

parameters.description: Filter by session id origin (agent, portal, script, transport)
parameters.name: kind

parameters.description: Sessions with activity after this time (RFC 3339)
parameters.name: start_time

parameters.description: Sessions with activity before this time (RFC 3339)
parameters.name: end_time

parameters.description: Only sessions that saved at least one asset
parameters.name: has_assets

parameters.description: Only sessions with at least one failed call
parameters.name: has_failures

get.description: Returns one session: its summary, the assets and insights it produced, and a page of its call timeline with the purpose stated for each call.

Returns the knowledge review-queue staleness alert configuration. Before an operator has written one, the platform defaults are returned with no recipients, and warnings state that nothing will be delivered.

put.description: Upserts the knowledge review-queue staleness alert configuration: the pending-count and age thresholds, the re-alert cooldown, and the recipients the digest is delivered to.

get.description: Returns the stored SMTP configuration. The password is never returned; password_set reports whether one is stored.

put.description: Upserts the SMTP configuration. The password is encrypted at rest; sending an empty password keeps the stored one.

get.description: Reports whether the given address has opted out of notification emails. Informational only; a test send is never blocked by it.
get.summary: Notification opt-out state of an address

post.description: Delivers a test email through the stored SMTP settings so the configuration can be verified end to end.

get.description: Returns platform identity, version, runtime feature availability, and config mode.
Returns all registered tools across all toolkits and platform-level tools.

post.description: Executes a tool via the MCP server and returns the result.

get.description: Returns JSON schemas for all registered tools including parameter definitions.

Returns everything the admin Tools page needs to render a single tool: kind, toolkit, connection, schema, per-persona allow/deny matrix with matched pattern, hidden state, description-override status, recent audit aggregate, and enrichment-rule count for gateway-proxied tools.

put.description: Adds or removes the named tool from the platform-wide tools.deny list. The deny list controls visibility in tools/list responses; persona auth gates execution independently. Read-modify-write through the standard config_entries store, so the value is JSON-encoded as []string and persists across restarts.

get.description: Returns known users (people seen via authentication or pre-added by an admin) for sharing.

parameters.description: Case-insensitive match on email or name
parameters.name: q

post.description: Pre-adds a person by email so they are selectable for sharing before they have logged in. Only available in database config mode.

get.description: Returns the api-kind connections the caller's persona reaches, each with the number of operations the route policy permits them.
get.summary: List the API connections you reach

get.description: Returns every operation of one api-kind connection that the caller's route policy permits, with the connection's upstream root and auth mode.
Returns one operation's parameters, request body and per-status responses, resolved exactly as api_get_endpoint_schema resolves them. An operation the route policy denies is reported as not found.

parameters.description: Component spec, when one id is defined by several
parameters.name: spec

get.description: Returns activity breakdown grouped by a dimension (tool_name, user_id, persona, toolkit_kind, or connection).
Returns aggregate activity metrics for the current user within an optional time range.
Returns time-bucketed activity data for the current user.

parameters.description: Bucket resolution: minute, hour, day (default: hour)
parameters.name: resolution

get.description: Returns paginated assets owned by the current user with optional filtering.

post.description: Creates a new asset by uploading inline text content (markdown, HTML, SVG, JSON, etc.). Use this to snapshot generated content into the asset portal without going through the MCP save_asset tool.

get.description: Ranks the current user's saved assets by relevance to q. Uses hybrid (semantic + lexical) ranking when an embedding provider is configured, falling back to lexical-only otherwise. Always scoped server-side to the requesting user's own assets.
Returns a single asset by ID. Non-owners need share access.

put.description: Updates the asset's name, description, or tags. The owner, an admin, or an asset Editor.

delete.description: Soft-deletes an asset. The owner or an admin.

get.description: Downloads the asset's binary content from S3.

put.description: Uploads new binary content for the asset, creating a new version.

parameters.description: Change summary for the new version
parameters.name: X-Change-Summary

post.description: Creates an independent copy of a shared asset in the current user's My Assets.

get.description: Returns what an asset's content references -- managed resources and other assets -- with enough of each target to render a row, the URL the reference is served under, and where the asset's stored content still writes the URI. A reference whose target was deleted is returned flagged as broken.

post.description: Adds one managed resource or one asset to the asset's references, checked against the caller's own read permission on that target. The asset's stored content is not changed. Returns the asset's references after the add.
post.summary: Add a reference to an asset

delete.description: Removes one reference from the asset. The asset's stored content is not changed, so a URI still written in the markup stops resolving. Returns the asset's references after the removal.
delete.summary: Remove one of an asset's references

get.description: Returns all shares for an asset. The owner or an admin.

post.description: Creates a share link or user-targeted share for an asset. The owner or an admin.

get.description: Count of stakeholders who signed off (N) out of the total stakeholders (M = owner + active share grantees).

Downloads the asset's PNG thumbnail image. The dark variant
falls back to the light/default thumbnail when none was captured.

put.description: Uploads a PNG thumbnail image for the asset.

delete.description:
Discards the asset's stored thumbnails so a fresh capture is
taken. The asset returns to the pending-thumbnail list.

get.description: Returns the assets whose content references this asset and which the caller may open, flagging any that carry an active public link share. Referencing assets the caller cannot open are counted but not named.
Returns paginated version history for an asset.
Downloads the binary content of a specific asset version.

post.description: Reverts the asset content to a specific version by creating a new version with that content.

get.description: Returns the calling user's own data-access calls, newest first: every query and API invocation the platform recorded, with the purpose stated for it and the outcome derived from what was built from it. There is no user parameter; the listing is always the caller's own.

parameters.description: Filter by outcome (failed, satisfied, superseded, ran)
parameters.name: outcome

parameters.description: Filter by a dataset URN or endpoint the call addressed
parameters.name: target

parameters.description: Match the purpose or the statement
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Set to 'promotable' for the records awaiting promotion, most reused first
parameters.name: queue

get.description: Returns one of the caller's own call records: the statement or request line, the purpose stated for it, its outcome and how it was reached, the assets and captures built from it, and how many later sessions re-ran it. A record id belonging to another user is not found, the same answer an id that was never used gets.

post.description: Publishes a satisfied record: a query becomes a Query entity in the data catalog, associated with every dataset it reads; an API call becomes a saved example on its endpoint. The record then carries what it became. Only the caller's own records can be promoted here, and only a record that answered something and has not already been promoted or declined.
Records that the caller decided this record is not worth publishing, with an optional note, so it stops being offered for promotion.

get.description: Returns paginated collections owned by the current user.

post.description: Creates a new collection for the current user.

get.description: Ranks the current user's collections by relevance to q (matching name, description, and section titles/descriptions). Uses hybrid (semantic + lexical) ranking when an embedding provider is configured, falling back to lexical-only otherwise. Always scoped server-side to the requesting user's own collections.
Returns a single collection by ID. Non-owners need share access.

put.description: Updates a collection's name and/or description. The owner, an admin, or a collection Editor.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a collection. The owner or an admin; an Editor share does not grant deletion.

put.description: Updates the collection's display configuration. The owner, an admin, or a collection Editor.
Replaces all sections and items in a collection. The owner, an admin, or a collection Editor.

get.description: Returns all shares for a collection. The owner or an admin.

post.description: Creates a share link or user-targeted share for a collection. The owner or an admin; an Editor share does not grant re-sharing.

get.description: Count of stakeholders who signed off (N) out of the total stakeholders (M = owner + active share grantees).
Downloads the collection's PNG thumbnail image.

put.description: Uploads a PNG thumbnail image for the collection. The owner, an admin, or a collection Editor.

get.description: Lists feedback threads across every asset, collection, and prompt the caller can view (owned or shared), most recent activity first. Each row carries the target's display label so the client can link back to it. Scoped server-side to the caller's accessible items, so it never discloses feedback on items the caller cannot see.
Returns canonical, org-shared knowledge pages. Open to every authenticated user.

post.description: Creates a canonical, org-shared knowledge page. Requires apply_knowledge access (the same authorization that applies captured insights).

get.description: Reverse lookup: returns the knowledge pages that reference the given entity (by serialized URN), so an entity view can surface "N knowledge pages reference this". Returns empty for an entity the viewer cannot access.
get.summary: List knowledge pages that reference an entity

get.description: Returns the knowledge pages and the entities they reference as typed nodes and edges, for the portal's graph view. Entities the viewer cannot access are absent (neither node nor edge), the same visibility rule the per-page refs and backlinks reads apply. Node and page caps are reported via truncated/notice rather than applied silently.
get.summary: The knowledge corpus as a graph

parameters.description: Only include pages carrying this tag
parameters.name: tag

parameters.description: Maximum pages to include (default and max 100)
parameters.name: limit

post.description: Resolves a batch of serialized reference URNs (mcp:/urn:li:) to a display label, type, and whether the target still exists, so the renderer can show named chips.
post.summary: Resolve entity references to display labels

post.description: Un-hides the platform's built-in knowledge pages a deployment hid, refreshed to the running release. Requires apply_knowledge access.

get.description: Ranks knowledge-page content by relevance to the query. Uses semantic ranking when an embedding provider is configured, else degrades to lexical-only. Open to every authenticated user.
Returns a single canonical knowledge page by id. Open to every authenticated user.

put.description: Replaces a knowledge page's content and records a new version. Requires apply_knowledge access.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a knowledge page. Requires apply_knowledge access.

get.description: Returns the insights the page was synthesized from and the promotion changesets that produced it (#678), so a reviewer can trace canonical knowledge back to the captured insights.
Returns the entities the page references (assets, prompts, collections, connections, DataHub URNs, and other pages), each with its serialized URN.
get.summary: List a knowledge page's entity references

put.description: Replaces the page's manually-authored references with the given set (parsed from serialized URNs). References carried from promotion (source=promoted) are preserved. Requires apply_knowledge access.
put.summary: Set a knowledge page's manual entity references

get.description: Returns the saved versions of a knowledge page, newest first. Open to every authenticated user.
get.summary: List a knowledge page's version history

get.description: Returns paginated insights captured by the current user.

Ranks the current user's knowledge insights by relevance to q. Uses hybrid (semantic + lexical) ranking when an embedding provider is configured, falling back to lexical-only otherwise. Always scoped server-side to the requesting user.
Returns aggregate statistics for the current user's insights.
